executive_summary: The S&P 500 closed above 7,000 for the first time and the Nasdaq posted its 12th consecutive gain — the longest streak since 2009 — fueled by growing optimism around a second round of US-Iran ceasefire talks and TSMC blockbuster Q1 earnings. TSMC reported 58% profit growth, raised full-year revenue guidance to 30%+, and confirmed AI chip demand is outstripping capacity — validating the $650 billion hyperscaler capex cycle. However, the ceasefire expires April 21 with no second round of talks scheduled, Brent crude sits at $98 with the Strait of Hormuz still blockaded, and March CPI spiked to 3.3% YoY (from 2.4%) driven by a 21.2% surge in gasoline prices. The Fed holds rates at 3.50-3.75% with the next decision April 28-29, and sticky inflation could shift the narrative from when do they cut to do they hike.

macro_events.title: Iran Ceasefire Expiry — April 21 Deadline Approaching
macro_events.causal_chain: Two-week ceasefire agreed April 8 expires April 21 → first round of talks collapsed after 21 hours → US naval blockade on Iranian ports continues → Strait of Hormuz carries 20% of global oil and 20% of LNG → war-risk insurance premiums on VLCCs remain elevated → Asian refiners rerouting via Cape of Good Hope (+12-14 days, +$2M/trip) → Qatar LNG to Europe at risk → if ceasefire lapses: Brent spikes past $110, tanker rates surge, airline fuel costs spike → if ceasefire extends/deal reached: Brent crashes to $75-80, energy sector sells off 10-15%, broader market rallies on inflation relief
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Global — Middle East, Asia-Pacific refining, European energy security, USD/commodity currencies
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq attack — Brent surged 15% in 24 hours, tanker rates ran 20-35% in one week, but reversed within 2 weeks as Saudi restored capacity
macro_events.counterargument: 40-country virtual summit Friday shows unprecedented diplomatic pressure for resolution; both sides have economic incentives to reopen Hormuz. Irans economy is cratering under blockade.

macro_events.title: March CPI Spike to 3.3% — Energy-Driven Inflation Re-Acceleration
macro_events.causal_chain: March CPI +0.9% MoM (+3.3% YoY, up from 2.4% in Feb) → energy index +10.9%, gasoline +21.2% accounting for 75% of monthly increase → Iran war / Hormuz blockade directly causing energy price surge → shelter still rising +0.3% → food +2.7% YoY → Fed funds at 3.50-3.75% with next meeting April 28-29 → if ceasefire fails and oil stays elevated, April CPI could hit 4%+ → Fed forced to pause rate cut expectations indefinitely, possibly signal hike risk → bond market bear steepener (10Y at 4.29%, 2Y at 3.78%, spread +54bp) reflects term premium repricing
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US domestic inflation, Fed policy, global bond markets
macro_events.historical_analog: 2022 inflation spike from Russia-Ukraine war — CPI hit 9.1% in June 2022, Fed hiked aggressively to 5.25-5.50%, S&P fell 25% from peak
macro_events.counterargument: Core CPI (ex-energy, food) likely still moderating — the spike is almost entirely energy-driven and would reverse quickly if Hormuz reopens.
